name: Pipeline inline inspection (MFL, ultrasonic, EMAT pigs)
aliases: Pipeline inline inspection (MFL, ultrasonic, EMAT pigs)
applications: integrity management of oil, gas and CO2 pipelines
principle: Instrumented pigs travel with the product and record wall loss, cracks and geometry. MFL is the most common and inexpensive method; ultrasonic tools measure wall thickness accurately but are costly; EMAT tools find cracks and stress-corrosion cracking without couplant.

process_steps.name: Launch smart pig from a trap

source.note: PHMSA Government/Industry Pipeline R&D Forum, technologies for pipeline inspection (older presentation; text partly garbled)

performance.metric: gas-coupled ultrasonic wall thickness accuracy (under development)
performance.basis: versus 10% for MFL, per the presentation

source.note: PHMSA Government/Industry Pipeline R&D Forum, technologies for pipeline inspection (older presentation; text partly garbled)

advantages: Different tools cover cracks and dents
limitations: The presentation is old and partly garbled; thresholds and the share of piggable lines are not stated
Unpiggable lines need other methods such as RFEC or direct assessment
